newsitem.title: USA: Kelly Flinn says she was victim of 'double standard'.
newsitem.headline: Kelly Flinn says she was victim of 'double standard'.

text.p: Former Lt. Kelly Flinn, who was discharged from the military for having an adulterous affair, said Sunday the treatment she received was indicative of a "double standard" in such cases, based on sex and rank.
In a guest essay appearing in the issue of Newsweek magazine which goes on sale Monday, Flinn compared her case to that of Air Force Gen. Joseph Ralston.

Ralston, who has been under consideration to become chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, has been supported by Defence Secretary William Cohen despite controversy over his admission that he had an adulterous affair years ago.

"I commend Secretary Cohen for taking a stand, for recognising that people do make mistakes and learn," Flinn said. But she said she had received no such support, and that "I sure wish that had happened to me."

"Our cases were very much the same, but we were treated very differently," Flinn said. "I don't know all the facts of Gen. Ralston's case, but I know enough to realise that in most important respects, we were in the same situation."
"This was all about our private lives. What we did had no effect on our performance in any way, shape or form," she said.
But she said their superiors had handled their cases very differently.

Flinn, the Air Force's first woman bomber pilot, was forced to leave the service last month without the honourable discharge she requested in order to avoid court-martial on charges of adultery, having sex with an enlisted man and lying about the matter.

"In Gen. Ralston's case, I don't know if his affair was even discussed with his superiors when it was going on. But I know that when it did come out, he got plenty of support and guidance. His superiors made an attempt to talk to him on a personal basis, to find out if his performance had been affected in some way," Flinn said.
"That certainly never happened in my case," she said.

Flinn said no one in her chain of command tried to talk to her about her problem. When she tried to discuss it with her commander he would not talk to her about it, telling her he expected he might have to be "the ultimate hammer," she said.
Flinn said she was treated differently than Ralston because of a double standard. "What matters in these cases is not what really happened, but your rank, your gender and who do you know," she said.

She added that she had personal knowledge of other people having affairs, and that such cases are not "isolated." She said she hoped some good would come from the notoriety of her case and the "public humiliation" she went through.
"I hope it opens the military's eyes and the public's eyes," she said. "We need more sensible rules. When it comes to consensual sex, the rule should be don't ask, don't tell."
